row_composite_model.method: 10-Lens Weighted Rest-of-World (ROW) Assumed Price Benchmark (Solving Rotterdam Spot Illiquidity vs China Export Bifurcation)
row_composite_model.summary: Combines all 10 physical, netback, econometric, incentive cost-floor, and structural balance signals into a single executable Rest-of-World (ex-China) assumed tungsten price of $1,717/mtu ($151,988/t APT). Weights Ex-China physical spot & contract clearing at 30% (M0 Rotterdam 16% + M4 Western Executable 14%), econometric lead & value-chain nowcasts at 44% (M4 Global Fair 13% + M8 VECM Lead 11% + M3 Value-Chain 10% + M2 Pure-Play Equities 10%), and physical netback, incentive cost floor & structural balance anchors at 26% (M9 Downstream 8% + M7 Incentive 6% + M5 Stock-to-Use 6% + M1 China Landed Parity 6%). Cross-checked across 4 aggregation methodologies: Arithmetic Weighted ($1,717/mtu), Log-Geometric Mean ($1,715/mtu), Bates-Granger Inverse-Variance Precision ($2,191/mtu), and Trimmed Mean ($1,589/mtu).

legacy_flaws: Contaminated Basket: Included non-tungsten HK stocks (1124.HK Coastal Greenland real estate, 0697.HK Shoucheng parking/infra) and copper giant 603993.SS CMOC (monthly corr = -0.069 with EU APT), producing a negative 21-day lead correlation of -0.1968.
Arithmetic Volatility Drag & Late-Listing Backfill: Compounded equal-weighted daily arithmetic returns and backfilled OTC ticker GMTL (listed March 2026) back to Jan 2025.

Ad-Hoc Functional Form & Retransformation Bias: Mapped index gains through an arbitrary curve without econometric calibration or Duan smearing, understating conditional mean by ~2% via Jensen's inequality.
v4_fixes: Verified Pure-Play Universe (All 12 Stocks Weighted & USD-Normalized): Chinese Producers (002378.SZ Zhangyuan 17%, 600549.SS Xiamen 12%, 000657.SZ CTHT 8%), Western Producers/Developers (EQR.AX 13%, GMET.L 10%, ALM 10%, TUN.L 7%, FWZ.V 7%, TGN.AX 4%, G6M.AX 3%), and Downstream Tooling Majors (KMT 5%, SAND.ST 4%).
Strong Positive Lead Signal: Clean USD log-return index leads European APT by 21 trading days (4 weeks) with r = +0.6015.

Centered Cointegrated Regression with Duan (1983) Smearing: Regresses log(APT) on the 3 log-return sub-baskets with interior economic elasticities, achieving R² = 0.9182 and smearing factor 1.0324, nowcasting $1,517/mtu.

legacy_flaws: Uncorrelated Macro Proxies: Regressed tungsten returns on Copper (HG=F, r = -0.165), S&P 500 (^GSPC, r = -0.312), FXI China Large-Cap (r = -0.061), and Iron Ore (TIO=F, r = +0.059). Generic macro assets did not experience China’s Feb 2025 dual-use tungsten export controls.

Explosive Intercept Drift ($7,739/mtu): Because the macro factors had ~0 explanatory power, OLS dumped the entire 9x tungsten rally into the monthly intercept (+11.96%/mo) and compounded it daily without mean reversion, exploding to $7,739/mtu.
Circular Smoothing in V2 Draft: Attempted to hide negative regression R² (-0.428) by blending 97.5% step + 2.5% (0.5*M0 + 0.5*M1), creating circular dependence on M0.
v4_fixes: Physical Value-Chain & Industrial Factors (Zero Circularity with M0): Replaced generic macro proxies with European Ferrotungsten ($/mtu-eq), China 65% Concentrate ($/mtu), China Tungsten Powder ($/mtu-eq), and Western Hardmetal Tooling/Strategic Metals (KMT + SAND.ST + REMX).

Econometric Validation: Monthly log-return regression R² improved from -0.428 to +0.5446 (with zero intercept drift), while the centered cointegrated level model achieves R² = 0.8550 with interior elasticities and Duan smearing (1.0629).

Actionable Valuation Insight: Nowcasts $1,389/mtu because European FeW ($152.5/kg = $1,209/mtu-eq) and Chinese Concentrate/Powder have cooled 50–65% from their March 2026 peaks, signaling that Rotterdam APT ($2,700/mtu) carries a ~$1,311/mtu illiquidity/vessel-shortage premium.

new_models_v4.m7_incentive: Marginal cost curve floor (90th-percentile smelting AISC ~$502/mtu) + Western greenfield capital recovery ($185/mtu) + convex inventory scarcity rent derived from M5 stock-to-use coverage.
new_models_v4.m8_vecm: Vector Error Correction Model fusing cointegrated anchor with 21-day lead returns of Equities, European FeW, and China Concentrate.
new_models_v4.m9_downstream: ITIA end-use weighted value-in-use netback parity across Cemented Carbide (62%), Specialty Steel & Superalloy FeW (24%), and Defense DFARS procurement (14%).

data_hygiene_audit.issue: Initial regex scraping of CTIA articles matched retrospective monthly/quarterly average articles ("Average Price from January to August"), low-grade 17% tungsten slime auction quotes, and "ferrotungsten powder" substrings, causing false single-day spikes.
data_hygiene_audit.fix: Filtered strictly to 413 daily market analysis reports, stripped lookback/threshold clauses, added negative lookbehinds for ferrotungsten/carbide powder, and parsed multi-product "respectively" clauses across all 6 physical streams (1,769 verified observations, 0 false single-day reversals across all 6 streams).

base.note: Base: demand CAGR 2.0% (Merchant Research & Consulting via deck), documented Western additions on schedule, ~6 kt of deck-implied "second wave" supply by 2032, policy premium decays through 2033.

bull.note: Bull: demand CAGR 3.0% (defense build-up, semiconductors/AI, EV), Sangdong II/Gentung delayed ~1 yr, second-wave supply halved and late, premium decays slowly (policy persists).

bear.note: Bear: demand CAGR 1.0% (global slowdown, substitution), additions accelerated (Gentung 2028), 12 kt second-wave supply by 2031, premium unwinds fast.

caveats: Inventory is invisible: global tungsten stocks are not publicly reported. The initial stock (3.0 months coverage at end-2024) is a calibration guess and the entire stock series is MODELED, not observed; errors compound over the forecast horizon.

Policy shocks dominate: China export controls (effective 4-Feb-2025), US DoW military procurement ban on China/Russia/NK tungsten (1-Jan-2027) and any new controls can override a balance model. The 2025-26 price explosion is mostly a policy/fragmentation premium (coverage only fell ~3.0 -> ~2.0 months), not pure balance.

Single-source deficits: the 5,570 t (2025) / 2,330 t (2026) figures come from the Sangdong NI 43-101 technical report quoted in Almonty marketing materials — one, potentially biased source; not independently verified.
USGS consumption data ends 2017; the long-run price/balance relationship is inferred from partial history and the deck-cited normal band (~$283-$642/mtu 2012-2017).

The "second wave" supply term (6-12 kt of unnamed supply by 2031-2035) is required to close the deck's own supply-gap chart but is NOT an announced project list. If it does not materialise, the late-decade re-tightening shown in base/bull is worse.
Demand price-elasticity (0.03-0.08) and the premium decay path are labelled estimates; they are the two least-observable parameters and drive most of the 2028+ spread.
Scenario tool for the Tungsten Desk dashboard — NOT investment advice.
supply_demand.headline: The 2025-26 tungsten spike ($330 -> ~$3,140/mtu) is reproduced as a stock-to-use squeeze amplified by a policy premium: the known 5.6 kt (2025) and 2.3 kt (2026) deficits drew modeled stocks from ~3.0 to ~1.9 months of coverage, and even a strongly convex balance curve cannot explain a 10x price move from that alone — export-control fragmentation, panic buying and defense stockpiling carry most of the move and decay into the early 2030s. Base case: price stays elevated (~$2,000-2,600) through 2027, then normalizes into the $850-1,500 range by 2029-2033 as documented Western supply (Sangdong I/II, Panasqueira L4, Gentung) plus ~6 kt of unnamed supply lands, with a re-tightening after 2033 if demand keeps compounding ~2% against a finite supply ramp. Bull (3% demand, delays): chronic $2,500-3,700 tightness through 2035. Bear (1% demand, accelerated supply): premium unwinds to a ~$300 floor by 2030-31. Confidence is LOW beyond ~2027: inventory is unobserved, the deficit anchors are single-source, and policy can override the balance at any time.
